lines.text: Warm? Third's warm, aye. Hands know it before I'm off the second ladder. Comes off the vents, that.
Pyrelisk? Up the vent line when it flares. Took the hair off my arm, the once.
Come round this side and say it again. Left ear's no good since the fourth shaft.
Right. A vent opens, the ground round it goes soft, and soft ground is what we cut. The housing went up behind it, which is why the east row leans. Mind the loose bit by the winch.
The shrines. We didn't put them there and we don't move them.
Ashvole burrow, and where they've been at the cinder it's loose enough to open a face.
Young men in good coats, in the front room, with a folder each.
One of them kept his gloves on indoors in high summer, in a room with a fire going in it, and I have never worked out why.

There were Stonewing on the west scarp when I was a girl, and Cragmar grazing the flat below them. If you say they went in the third contract, that will be right. If you say the second, I'd not argue with you either.
The mine's boring.
There's a shrine at the bottom of the third shaft bigger than a cart. I've not seen it and nobody's taking me down.
Sable's Pyrelisk is loud. Was that all you wanted? Only I was doing something.
The overalls are company issue and there's no company here to issue them.
West scarp crew. Six-year contract, came in on weight in four. I was on it, I took the early bonus and I spent it, and I'm not going to tell you I didn't.
My wife was born here, three doors up from where we live now.
Watch that crate, the lid's off. They come open on their own now and the Carricrow have worked that out.
Contract's shut, so I'm pulling cable and rail out, and you can follow the cable runs the whole way up from the vent line. I'll walk you up if you've a morning to give it.
There's a rail up top that four of us couldn't shift, and it's still up there, and I have a go at it most mornings going past, on my own, which tells you how that goes.
First time up here? There's a kettle on at the hut if you want a cup before you go up.

The warden's up and down this scarp with a book under her arm, and I was on the crew that worked it, right to the end. Quiet in the middle of the day, and it ought to be. Come dusk it's quiet as well now, and it never used to be.
More Carricrow than there used to be, and there were Stonewing lifting off that rock when I started.
The nest on the west scarp is empty and I go past it every time I'm up for the rail, with nothing on it and nothing round it, and the white streak underneath has gone grey.
